A1.title: Context Logic
A1.description: The module describes the structure, function, and effect of context in the Behavioral Change Model (BCM) 2.0. Context is not an environment, but a structurally effective space in which utility effects can only be realized, inhibited, or changed.
A1.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

scope.temporal_scope: time-point-based and dynamic simulations (ΔC over t)
scope.modularity: applicable in all BCM2 and BCM3 complementary modules
scope.restrictions: only initializable when Awareness (7240), Willingness (7243), and Segment Logic modules (7257) are active

goals: Assessment of segment-relational effects and context elasticity
Integration of context axes in utility, awareness, and complementarity logic
Calculation of context-modulated thresholds and reactions
purpose_and_function.functional_role: The module operationalizes the contextual effect level at which individual, collective, and identity utility functions are realized or inhibited.

KON_Axioms.title: Context is not utility, but structurally effective impact horizon
KON_Axioms.description: Context influences behavior and utility realization, but is not itself a utility function. It forms the structural impact horizon in which utility functions only become effective or remain inhibited. Its effect varies over time, stability, and epistemic coherence.
KON_Axioms.formalization: U_i(t) = f(INU_i, KNU_i, IDN_i | C⃗(t), α_control, Bias(E1–E5)) with U_i ≠ C⃗(t) ∧ ∂U_i/∂C⃗ ≠ 0
implications: Context defines the structural conditions for utility realization.
Any change in context changes the realization probability of U_i(t).
Epistemic distortions (E1–E5) modulate the perception of context effect.
High institutional stability (α_control) reduces context sensitivity.

parameters.U_i(t): Total utility of actor i over time t

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: Context acts mediated and structurally feedback-coupled
KON_Axioms.description: Context influences behavior through modulation functions such as complementarity, awareness, and decision thresholds, but simultaneously acts structurally back on behavior through the dynamic context function Ω(C⃗,t,α_control,ψ,Bias). This describes systemic drift, resonance, and stability damping between behavior and context over time.
KON_Axioms.formalization: V_i(t+1) = f(U_i(t), κ(C⃗,t), A_mod(C⃗,t), θ_i(C⃗,t), Ω(C⃗,t,α_control,ψ,Bias)) with ∂V_i/∂C⃗ ≠ 0
implications: Context primarily acts through mediating functions like complementarity, awareness, and thresholds, but additionally possesses structural feedback.
Ω(C⃗,t,α_control,ψ,Bias) models contextual drift and institutional resonance.
High institutional stability (α_control) reduces feedback strength.
Epistemic distortions (Bias E1–E5) can over- or underestimate feedback.
ψ(C⃗,t) functions as damping coefficient for contextual resonance effects.

parameters.V_i(t): Behavior of actor i at time t
parameters.U_i(t): Utility value of actor i at time t
parameters.A_mod(C⃗,t): Awareness modulation via context and time
parameters.Ω(C⃗,t,α_control,ψ,Bias): Dynamic context function (drift, resonance, stability, distortion)
parameters.α_control: Degree of institutionalization of divergence – structural stability parameter
parameters.Bias(E1–E5): Epistemic distortion on perception and context evaluation

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: Context is vectorial, multidimensional, structure-typed, and dynamically feedback-coupled
KON_Axioms.description: The context of a system is understood as a dynamic, vectorial space C⃗(t) consisting of multiple dimensions c_i. Each dimension represents an independent structural effect level (institutional, social, symbolic, technical, physical, media, etc.) and is modulated over time, resonance ψ(C⃗,t), stability α_control, and epistemic distortion Bias(E1–E5).
KON_Axioms.formalization: C⃗(t) = { (c_i, w_i, τ_i(t), α_control_i, ψ_i(t), Bias_i(E1–E5)) | i = 1,…,n; Σw_i = 1 } ∧ dC⃗/dt ≠ 0

parameters.C⃗(t): Total context vector at time t
parameters.c_i: Individual dimension of context (e.g., institutional, social, symbolic)
parameters.τ_i(t): Time dependency or inertia of the dimension
parameters.α_control_i: Institutional stability of the respective axis (0–1)
parameters.ψ_i(t): Resonance coefficient of axis i over time t
parameters.Bias_i(E1–E5): Epistemic distortion of perception of this axis

implications: Context consists of dynamically weighted dimensions whose effects can be time-dependent, resonant, and epistemically distorted.
High α_control stabilizes individual dimensions against drift but reduces adaptability.
ψ(C⃗,t) allows modeling of resonance or damping effects between dimensions.
Bias(E1–E5) explains divergent perceptions of the same context dimension.
The vectorial context forms the basis for φ(C⃗,t), χ(C⃗,t,S), and Ω(C⃗,t).
KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: Complementarities are context-modulated, segment-relative, and dynamically feedback-coupled
KON_Axioms.description: The strength and direction of complementarities between utility functions U_i and U_j depend on the structure, dynamics, stability, and perception of context. Context axes C⃗(t) modulate the interaction through the function φ(C⃗,t,S,ψ,Bias). Resonance ψ(C⃗,t) and stability α_control determine whether complementarities are amplified, damped, or become unstable.

parameters.Comp(U_i,U_j|C⃗,t,S): Current complementarity between utility functions in segment S
parameters.φ(C⃗,t,S,ψ,Bias): Context, time, segment, and perception modulation function
parameters.α_control: Degree of institutionalization of divergence (stability coefficient)
parameters.ψ(C⃗,t): Resonance coefficient between utility functions in context
parameters.ε(...): Residual term for nonlinear resonance and damping effects

implications: Complementarity is dynamic, segment-dependent, and modulable through context resonance ψ(C⃗,t).
High context drift (Ω) leads to unstable complementarity.
Institutional stability (α_control) dampens resonance and stabilizes cooperation effects.
Epistemic distortions (Bias E1–E5) lead to asymmetric perceptions of the same relation.
φ(C⃗,t,S,ψ,Bias) connects structural and psychological context levels.
KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: Awareness is context-dependent, dynamic, and segment-relational
KON_Axioms.description: The probability and intensity of awareness depends on the structure and dynamics of context as well as segment affiliation. Awareness emerges through resonance between context axes C⃗(t) and segment-relative perception filters ω_S.
KON_Axioms.formalization: P(A=1 | C⃗,t,S) = χ(C⃗,t,S,α_control) = σ(β₀ + Σ β_i·C_i(t) + γ_S + δ·Ω(C⃗,t) - η·Bias(E1–E5))

parameters.C⃗(t): Context vector at time t (institutional, social, symbolic, etc.)
parameters.S: Segment identity or collective perception structure
parameters.α_control: Degree of institutionalization of divergence – measures stability of perception order
parameters.Ω(C⃗,t): Context drift or rate of change of context axes
parameters.Bias(E1–E5): Perception bias arising from the difference between individual, collective, and institutional levels

implications: Awareness emerges through resonance between context dynamics and segment-relative perception.
High context drift (Ω) can destabilize awareness when α_control is low.
Institutionally stable systems (high α_control) reduce Bias(E1–E5) and stabilize awareness.
Awareness is not binary but a continuous, time-dependent variable.

examples.high_awareness_context: α_control=0.8, Ω=0.1 → stable awareness with moderate context change
examples.low_awareness_context: α_control=0.3, Ω=0.4 → awareness fluctuates strongly, segment reactions diverge

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: Context acts segment-relationally and perception-differentiated
KON_Axioms.description: Segments react differently to the same context because their internal perception functions ω_S and awareness profiles χ(C⃗,t,S) differ. Context effect is thus relational and dependent on segment-internal coherence, institutional stability (α_control), and perception bias (E1–E5).
KON_Axioms.formalization: V_i(S_a,t) = f(U_i, C⃗,t, ω_Sa, χ(C⃗,t,Sa), α_control, Bias(E1–E5)) ≠ V_i(S_b,t) = f(U_i, C⃗,t, ω_Sb, χ(C⃗,t,Sb), α_control, Bias(E1–E5)) for S_a ≠ S_b

parameters.V_i(S,t): Behavior function of individual i in segment S at time t
parameters.U_i: Utility vector of individual i (INU, KNU, IDN)
parameters.ω_S: Segment-internal perception filter – defines weighting of context axes
parameters.α_control: Degree of institutionalization of divergence (coherence stabilizer)

implications: Context has no uniform effect; perception is segment-relative.
Different segments use different perception filters ω_S(C⃗).
High α_control reduces perception divergences between segments.
Segmented awareness creates segmented behavioral effects (V_i(S)).
Bias structures between E1–E5 can distort or amplify segment reactions.

examples.case_1: Two professional groups (physicians, nurses) experience the same organizational context differently due to different ω_S.
examples.case_2: Political segments react differently to media context depending on awareness level and social coherence.

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: Context dynamically and perception-dependently influences utility thresholds
KON_Axioms.description: The decision threshold θ_i of actor i is not a constant quantity but is modulated by the current context vector C⃗(t), individual awareness χ(C⃗,t,S), institutional stability (α_control), and perception bias (E1–E5).
KON_Axioms.formalization: θ_i(C⃗,t) = θ₀i + δ_i(C⃗,t) - λ·χ(C⃗,t,S) + κ·(1 - α_control) + η·Bias(E1–E5)

parameters.θ_i(C⃗,t): context- and time-dependent decision threshold of actor i
parameters.α_control: Degree of institutionalization of divergence – stability factor for thresholds
parameters.Bias(E1–E5): Perception distortion due to different epistemic levels

implications: Context changes shift decision thresholds dynamically.
Increased awareness (χ) lowers the threshold, increases action probability.
Low institutional stability (α_control) increases threshold volatility.
Epistemic distortions (Bias) lead to over- or underestimation of the threshold.
Thresholds are thus adaptive functions, not constant parameters.

examples.example_1: With stable institutions (α_control=0.8) and high awareness (χ=0.7), θ_i decreases by approx. 15%.
examples.example_2: With low stability (α_control=0.3) and strong context drift (Ω=0.4), θ_i increases significantly, decision inhibition.

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: Context is inertial, feedback-coupled, and dynamic
KON_Axioms.description: Context develops over time through feedback with behavior. Changes do not occur instantaneously but inertially and dependent on the resonance function ψ(C⃗,t), which describes sensitivity to behavior and institutional stability α_control.

parameters.C⃗(t): Vectorial context state at time t
parameters.ψ(C⃗,t,α_control): Resonance or reaction coefficient, dependent on context stability and degree of institutionalization
parameters.α_control: Stability parameter – how strongly institutional structures compensate context drift
parameters.Bias(E1–E5): Epistemic divergence that disturbs or distorts context resonance

implications: Context reacts with temporal delay to behavior – no simultaneous causality.
Institutional stability α_control dampens contextual resonance and stabilizes systems.
Bias(E1–E5) can distort feedback and over- or under-control resonance.
With high ψ and low α_control, chaotic context drifts emerge.
Context inertia is necessary to filter short-term behavioral changes.

examples.example_1: After a political shock (ΔV_t), media context changes only slowly because ψ=0.2 and α_control=0.9 (high stability).
examples.example_2: In an unstable system (α_control=0.3, ψ=0.8), the same event leads to massive context drift (ΔC=+0.6).

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: There is no context-neutral state
KON_Axioms.description: Every observable behavior is under the influence of a context. A context-free state does not exist; every behavioral variation implies a change in at least one context dimension.
implications: No behavior exists without context reference.
Every intervention changes at least one context dimension.
Context dependency is a necessary condition for all utility functions U_i.

parameters.∂V/∂C: partial derivative of behavioral change with respect to context

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.title: Context is only structurally changeable
KON_Axioms.description: Context changes arise exclusively through structural adjustments in institutions, rules, and norms. The speed and scope of these changes depend on the intervention elasticity Ω(C⃗,ΔI,α_control), which describes how sensitively the context reacts to institutional impulses.

parameters.ΔC⃗: Change of context vector over time (t → t+1)
parameters.Ω(C⃗,ΔI,α_control): Intervention elasticity – determines structural responsiveness of the system
parameters.α_control: Degree of institutionalization of divergence – describes stability
parameters.Bias(E1–E5): Epistemic distortion that influences structural adjustment

implications: Context change is a structure-driven, not behavioral process.
Rapid context transformation requires high intervention elasticity Ω.
Institutional stability (α_control) dampens the effect of structural interventions.
Epistemic distortions (Bias) can hinder or accelerate structural adjustment.
Behavioral changes without structural change produce no sustainable context shift.

examples.example_1: A company changes communication norms but not the hierarchy: ΔNorms>0, ΔInstitutions=0 → ΔC⃗ small.
examples.example_2: A state reforms institutions and laws simultaneously: high Ω → ΔC⃗ large, stabilizing effect.

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core

KON_Axioms.name: Salience of Context Factors
KON_Axioms.equation: Eff(C_i) = w_i · U (when S_i ≥ θ_S, else 0)
KON_Axioms.description: Only salient context factors are behaviorally relevant. Dynamic salience σ_dyn(C_i,t) allows time-dependent perception intensity as a function of context change.
KON_Axioms.notes: Extension integrates σ_dyn(C_i,t) = σ_0(C_i) + ρ · dC_i/dt. This function models habituation and reactivation of attention as a result of contextual dynamics. ρ is the reactivity coefficient, σ_0 is the base salience.

KON_Axioms.name: Tasks as Context
KON_Axioms.description: Activities are contextual elements of human behavior and are described via standardized dimensions. Relations between tasks can be complementary, substituting, or neutral.
KON_Axioms.aggregate_utility: U(S) = Σ U(Ti) + Σ δ * R(Ti,Tj|K) * min{U(Ti), U(Tj)}

KON_Axioms.name: Jobs as Task Combination
KON_Axioms.description: A job is a structured combination of task dimensions with weightings, relations, and temporal structure.

definition.utility_function: U(J) = Σ wi*U(Ti) + Σ δ * R(Ti,Tj|K) * min{wi*U(Ti), wj*U(Tj)}

KON_Axioms.name: Teams as Coordinated Job Combination
KON_Axioms.description: A team is a combination of individuals with different job profiles whose coordinated cooperation is necessary to fulfill a task in the required time and quality.

definition.utility_function: U(Θ) = Σ U(Jk) + Σ λ * C(Jk, Jl|K)

parameters.C: Relation between job profiles in context (synergy or conflict)

KON_Axioms.name: Departments as Structured Team Combination
KON_Axioms.description: A department is a combination of multiple teams aligned toward a common goal. Utility results from team utility plus coordination effects.

definition.utility_function: U(A) = Σ U(Θr) + Σ μ * C(Θr, Θs|K)

parameters.μ: Quality of department coordination (0 = poor, 1 = perfect)
parameters.C: Relation between teams in context (synergy or conflict)

KON_Axioms.name: Organizations as Coordinated Department Combination
KON_Axioms.description: An organization is a coordinated combination of multiple departments with shared governance, culture, and strategy.

definition.utility_function: U(O) = Σ U(Aq) + Σ ν * C(Aq, Ar|K) + G(O)

parameters.ν: Quality of organizational coordination (0 = weak, 1 = strong)
parameters.C: Relation between departments in context (synergy or conflict)
parameters.G(O): Governance and culture effects that shape overall utility

KON_Axioms.name: Networks and Ecosystems
KON_Axioms.description: Networks emerge through cooperation of multiple organizations. They are characterized by dependencies, alliances, and shared infrastructure.

definition.utility_function: U(N) = Σ U(Oi) + Σ ρ * C(Oi, Oj|K)

KON_Axioms.name: Societies and Markets
KON_Axioms.description: Societies emerge from the interaction of multiple networks and institutions. Markets are specific forms of societal coordination.

definition.utility_function: U(S) = Σ U(Ni) + Σ σ * C(Ni, Nj|K) + I(S)

parameters.σ: Quality of societal coordination (institutions, legal system, culture)

KON_Axioms.name: Multidimensionality of Rewards
KON_Axioms.description: Rewards that activate multiple utility axes simultaneously have stronger effects than one-dimensional rewards. Freedom of choice additionally amplifies the effect through IDN and KNU effects.

formalization.gift_bonus: ΔU_Gift = α * INU + β * KNU + γ * IDN

implications: One-dimensional rewards have weak effects (cash).
Multidimensional rewards create stronger effects (gift).
Freedom of choice amplifies total utility regardless of chosen option.

KON_Axioms.name: Freedom of Choice as Context Factor
KON_Axioms.description: Freedom of choice amplifies KNU and IDN but simultaneously increases complexity and uncertainty.

formalization.total_effect: ΔU_Choice = ΔU_Option + λ * (KNU + IDN) - φ * κ_choice(n, δ)

parameters.κ_choice(n, δ): Complexity costs as function of number of options n and ambiguity δ

implications: With few, clear options: Net effect positive (autonomy, fairness).
With many or difficult-to-compare options: Net effect negative (choice overload).
Curated choice or default options lower complexity costs and stabilize net effect.

KON_Axioms.title: Degree of Institutionalization of Divergence
KON_Axioms.definition: Systems possess a variable capacity to absorb and maintain stable divergent perception levels (E0–E5). This capacity describes the institutional mechanism that compensates context drift and maintains coherence.

functional_logic.interpretation: High resilience means that despite contextual drift, system coherence is maintained.

KON_Axioms.author: FehrAdvice & Partners AG – BCM Architecture Core
KON_Axioms.notes: KX21 extends context module 8904 with variable α_control according to AX 0.00j. Fully AOM-compliant, validated, and auditable.

conditions: Context axes must be specified or reconstructed as vector C(t).
Segment logic (BCM2_09_SEG7257) must be actively available.
Connection to A_mod(t), R(t), and ΔC(t) is required.
LLM-supported context extraction can be used when C⃗(t) is incomplete.

semantic_boundary.statement: Context is not individual belief, not decision, not motivation. It is structural effect space and not substitutable by utility logic.
semantic_boundary.implication: The module may not be used to model individual preference or motivation systems.
